The '''1994–95 Scottish Premier Division''' season began on 13 August 1994; it was the first season of the new ten team league format, and also the first season using the rule of awarding [[three points for a win]]. 

==Overview==
The 1994–95 Scottish Premier Division season ended in success for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who won the title by fifteen points from nearest rivals [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] to clinch seven titles in a row. [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] were relegated to the [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] after finishing bottom with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] surviving a relegation playoff against [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Motherwell were joined by [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] winners [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Fourth-placed [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] as [[Scottish Cup]] winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem96.htm|title=Scottish Premier Division 1995/96|publisher=Soccerbot|access-date=2008-06-04| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080514141514/http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem96.htm| archive-date= 14 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

The season began on 13 August with the first goal of the season scored by [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s [[Billy Findlay]] as they won 5–0 at home to Dundee United. The regular league season ended on 13 May, with the relegation/promotion play-off following on the 21st and 25th.

==Play-off==
A two leg play-off took place between the 9th placed team in the Premier Division (Aberdeen) and the runner-up of the [[1994–95 Scottish First Division|First Division]] ([[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]). Aberdeen won both legs by 3 goals to 1, winning the tie 6–2 on aggregate, thus securing their place in the [[1995–96 Scottish Premier Division]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/aberdeen-find-form-to-preserve-premier-status-1621213.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/aberdeen-find-form-to-preserve-premier-status-1621213.html |archive-date=2022-05-01 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Aberdeen find form to preserve Premier status|date=26 May 1995|access-date=27 October 2018|author=David McKinney|work=[[The Independent]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pictures-agony-ecstasy-scottish-football-5645260|title=In pictures: The agony and ecstasy of Scottish football play-off drama|last=Haggerty|first=Tony|date=6 May 2015|newspaper=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|access-date=1 October 2018}}</ref>
